texts.preamble: Aseena vs Kanjoor Grama Panchayat on 13 February, 2019 Author: Shaji P.Chaly Bench: Shaji P.Chaly In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present The Honourable Mr. Justice Shaji P.Chaly Wednesday,The 13Th Day Of February 2019 / 24Th Magha, 1940 WP(C).No. 2575 of 2019 Petitioner/S: Aseena, Aged 57 Years, W/O.Raghavan, Valloor House, Edavoor Kara, Koovappady Village, Kunnathunadu Taluk. By Advs. Sri.V.Rajendran (Perumbavoor) Sri.George Varghese Kizhakkambalam Sri.N.Rajesh Respondent/S: 1 Kanjoor Grama Panchayat, Kanjoor P.O., -683575, Represented By Its Secretary. 2 Secretary, Kanjoor Grama Panchayat, Kanjoor P.O., -683575. R1 & R2 By Advs. Sri.P.G.Jose Sri.V.A.Vinod This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Been Finally Heard On 13.02.2019, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following: WP(C).No. 2575 of 2019 2 Aseena vs Kanjoor Grama Panchayat on 13 February, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33481094/ 1 Judgment
texts.facts: This writ petition is filed by the petitioner seeking the following reliefs:- "i) To declare that the petitioner has got deemed license under the D & O Rules for conducting "Azad Margin Free Super Market" in sho No.II/159 of Kanjoor Grama Panchayat. ii) To issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ order or direction, directing the respondents to issue a certificate showing that the petitioner has got deemed license under the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act and D & O Rules for conducting Azad Margin Free Super Market in shop No.II/159 of Kanjoor Grama Panchayat. iii) To grant such other reliefs which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper in the circumstances of the case. 2. The case projected by the petitioner is that, the business was being conducted by the petitioner from the year 2012 onwards, after securing D & O license from the Secretary of the Panchayat. However, when the petitioner submitted the application for the year 2018-2019, the same was not issued and thereupon, petitioner has secured deemed license by virtue of Section 236(3) of the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994. 3. Anyway, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that, petitioner was continuing the business without any interference from the Panchayat, in view of the deemed license.
